correctness.rationale: The uniform-circle viewing direction has exact Jacobian density 1-r cos(theta)/sqrt(1-r^2 sin^2(theta)). This yields a contiguous n^-1/2 perturbation. The canonical uniform triple kernel has second Fourier eigenvalues ((-1)^k-1)/(2*pi^2*k^2); only first cosine shifts under the local alternative. The degenerate remainder vanishes at n^2, and the first projection under P_r has linear term 2r cos(theta)/pi^2, giving sharp outer Gaussian variance 1/(2*pi^4). Exact angular mean and all 924 independent numerical checks agree. No unjustified passage from finite enumeration to an infinite theorem occurs.

Other random-polygon U-max asymptotics concern extreme areas/perimeters, not the unnormalized count of query-containing triangles.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The theorem proved here is a strict statement refinement: under r_n=c/sqrt(n), centered at the fixed central null mean, one Fourier component acquires a c-dependent noncentral shift and the remaining components stay central; for r_n>>n^-1/2 the centered statistic is Gaussian with explicit variance 1/(2*pi^4). These claims are not stated in inspected accessible material. Some source full texts remain uninspected, so an unrecognized specialization is possible.

evidence: Killeen–Hettmansperger (2020 online) derive the null law and asymptotic null distribution of an origin-containing-triangle count under angular symmetry.
Jentsch–Nagy–Wendler (2026) describe degenerate center and nondegenerate fixed off-center evaluation, with an adaptive subsampling procedure.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A query offset from the center is equivalent to an origin query with displaced angular observation density, so both location-test and triangular-array formulations were compared. A fixed-noncentral-query central limit does not imply the exact rate n^-1/2 noncentral quadratic limit, and the null law itself does not imply it.

originality.rationale: The known central null spectrum, classic circle sampling and fixed-query depth dichotomy are expressly excluded from novelty. The surviving theorem gives a concrete local triangular-array distribution at radius c/sqrt(n), first-harmonic noncentrality, exact variance and an explicit Gaussian outer window. Comparative searches and material primary reading found no covering theorem; absence of accessible full texts of two closest papers is a residual, not proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: The full text of Killeen–Hettmansperger (2020/2021) was inaccessible, and its local-power analysis could contain a relevant special-case distribution not visible in the abstract.
The complete 2026 Jentsch–Nagy–Wendler manuscript was not accessible in a working HTML representation; its full theory could imply a variant of the moving query statement.
A complete bibliographic priority review is not possible; keyword and record searches alone do not establish uniqueness.

value.rationale: Central and off-center simplicial depth have different asymptotic normalizations. The derived exact transition at query displacement n^-1/2 addresses the mathematically natural unknown intermediate regime, yields a complete one-parameter noncentral family, an explicit outer Gaussian variance and exact population drift. This affects calibration of near-center depth-based location tests and is not a mere sign or normalization correction.
